title: Exact Fourier certificates for complex Hadamard matrices of order six
main_claim: Theorem 1 (Fourier vanishing): every complex Hadamard matrix H of order 6 that is not equivalent to Tao's cubic matrix T has g_H(πα)=0 for every permutation π of α=(1,1,1,-1,-1,-1). This proves the Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Weiner conjecture. Theorem 2: there are no 7 MUBs in C^6, so N(6)≤5 by Weiner's completion theorem. Both rest on exact rational certificates.
coverage:
I read the whole paper (sections 1–5) and the verifier. 
(1) Pair certificate (Prop 2.x): I checked it independently with floating-point numerics on 5 random order-6 Hadamard matrices from least-squares solutions (generic points), and on F6 and T. Over all 1440 (orientation, row-permutation) choices, max|L| and max|g(α)g(q)| were about 1e-16 for both values of q. Generic matrices and F6 also gave max|g(α)| about 1e-16. T has |g(α)|=1/2 and L=0, which is consistent with the dichotomy. 
(2) Dichotomy proof: I checked the permutation argument that gives g(2(e_i-e_j))=0 for all i≠j. 
(3) Cubic classification (Prop 3.1): I checked every step by hand: Newton's identities and the e_{6-k} relation; the support-intersection table and the x=y=-1 contradiction; the block-form exclusion via restricted spans and Cauchy–Schwarz; the 2-2-2 counts; the derivation s_ij=s_ji; the 2-regular graph on 5 vertices being a 5-cycle. 
(4) Cubic-pair exclusion: I recomputed with numerics that R(b)=λ_j G(b) on all 860 support charges, with λ=(1/2,3,9,4) and R=0 off those orbits. I also confirmed |G| is constant on every listed orbit, recomputed the orbit counts for w5+D and w8+D, and solved the linear system: S3=S7=1/10, S0=-4/5, 6+30S0=-18. 
(5) Mixed certificate: I checked the Gram lemma weights (5, and 1/4 for the F1F1 term), the singleton reduction coefficient -1/(7-l), the mixed-same/different equations against the code (mixeq), the exact-substitution lemma and the WP=0 check in eliminate, the Schur pivot check in posdef, and the tagmom/product weights. All match the paper. 
(6) I reran verification/run.py (54 s). It reproduces the stated rank tables and the final bound.
sibling_notes: Family 266 had no prior entries on the board. I can only check Theorem 2's mixed 7-MUB certificate (Prop 5.x) by reading the code: no 7-MUB instance exists to test it numerically. I read the code paths that matter and they are consistent with the paper's lemmas. The companion paper OpenAI2026MUBMaximum (N(6)=3) is cited only as context, so there is no circular dependence.
